The same model is available from Best Buy for $1,850, so it definitely makes sense to purchase it from Lenovo unless you happen across a big price cut at Best Buy.

There's one model above my test system in the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11. It has the same specs as the one I tested but comes with a superior display: a 2.8K OLED with a faster 120Hz refresh rate that's rated for 1,100 nits of brightness in HDR mode and 500 nits in SDR. It has a list price of $1,900 and was selling for $1,800.

The Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 starts at £1,082 in the UK and AU$1,999 in Australia.

Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 performance

With its Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2-E94-100 processor, featuring an 18-core CPU and an NPU capable of 80 TOPS, the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 achieved strong results across both our multicore and AI benchmarks. It's one of the few Windows laptops to top the M5 MacBook Air on the multicore Geekbench 6 test, and did so with ease, with a score of more than 19,000. It also pulled off the same feat on the multicore Cinebench 2024 test. Its single-core results weren't on the same level as its multicore scores but still above average.

It also outpaced the M5 MacBook Air on our Geekbench AI test, thanks to its 80 TOPS NPU. It's well equipped to perform local AI tasks, but for 3D performance, its integrated Qualcomm Adreno GPU can't compete with Intel models such as the Dell XPS 14 and MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI Plus that have integrated Intel Arc B390 graphics. Still, its score on 3Dmark Steel Nomad was close to that of the M5 MacBook Air's.

Matt Elliott/CNET

The Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 achieved this performance while also demonstrating strong efficiency, as we've seen from other Snapdragon X-series laptops. It lasted more than 22 hours in our YouTube streaming battery-drain test, providing around-the-clock mobility. Still, other laptops run even longer. The Intel Panther Lake-based MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI Plus lasted 3 hours longer on the test than the Yoga Slim 7x, and the Snapdragon X-based HP OmniBook 5 14 extends your time away from a power outlet to over 28 hours.

Compact and blue

The Yoga Slim 7x looks good and feels solid. The thin and compact, all-metal chassis is rigid with little flex, and it comes in a deep blue color that Lenovo calls Cosmic Blue. The color is a nice departure from basic silver, gray or black but isn't so loud that it would look out of place in an office or boardroom. As much as I like the color of the chassis, I don't like its ability to collect fingerprints and smudges.

While its trim dimensions make it easy to toss the Yoga Slim 7x into a backpack, it's a tad heavier than it looks. Its nearly 3-pound weight is average for a 14-inch laptop. It weighs substantially more than the 2.2-pound Asus Zenbook A14 and 2.2-pound Acer Swift Edge 14 AI and is closer in weight to the 2.9-pound HP OmniBook 5 and 2.7-pound MacBook Air 13.

Matt Elliott/CNET

I love the Yoga Slim 7x's keyboard, but am less enamored by its touchpad. The keyboard is excellent, in line with the company's top-notch ThinkPads. The keys offer a firm yet snappy feedback with a bit more travel than I expected for such a thin laptop. The travel isn't so deep that it'll slow you down, but instead provides more of a plush feel than the shallow travel of a MacBook's keyboard.

Meanwhile, the touchpad is merely serviceable. It's a standard mechanical touchpad with clicks that are harder to perform on the top half than near the bottom. I'd be willing to accept this mainstream feature on one of the lower-end configurations, but for my $1,700 test system, I'd like to get a haptic touchpad with a consistent (and customizable) click response across its entire surface.

Matt Elliott/CNET

Flanking the keyboard are two speaker grilles. Beneath each is a 2-watt tweeter, and these speakers are complemented by a pair of 2-watt woofers that fire from a slit on each side of the laptop. The sound is fuller than that of a typical laptop, with some separation evident between high and low tones and even a hint of bass response.

Lenovo offers two OLED options for the Yoga Slim 7x, and I got the lower-end one. The 1,920x1,200-pixel resolution creates reasonably sharp images and text, but it might be worth upgrading to the higher-res 2,880x1,800-pixel panel if you plan to use the laptop to stare at text all day. There's some slight text fuzziness and pixelation. Lenovo's pricing for the display upgrade is inconsistent. It's a no-brainer for the $60 Lenovo charges for the customizable model, but it's a more difficult proposition when it costs $200 to go from the config I tested to the same fixed config with the 2.8K OLED.

Still, the display I tested has the standard OLED goodies of vivid color and infinite contrast with effective zero-nit black levels. And its color performance was great. On my tests with a Spyder X colorimeter, it showed 100% coverage of the sRGB and P3 spaces and 95% of AdobeRGB. It also achieved 393 nits of peak brightness, which is a solid number for an OLED that doesn't need to get as bright as an LCD panel thanks to its aforementioned deep black level and stellar contrast.

Matt Elliott/CNET

The display's resolution may be pedestrian, but the webcam's is not. It's a 9.2-megapixel camera that produces crisp 4K photos and 1440p video. It's also an IR cam that you can use for Windows Hello facial recognition logins. Without a fingerprint reader on board, the webcam is the only method for secure biometric logins.

The port situation is grim. With just three USB4 ports, you'll need an adapter to connect even headphones, let alone devices that require a USB-A or HDMI port. But, hey, at least the USB4 ports are faster with 40Gbps transfer speeds.

Is the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 a good laptop?

The Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x is great if you want an easily portable OLED laptop with strong overall performance, but don't plan to lean into any heavy lifting in terms of 3D graphics work or gaming. With its Snapdragon X2 Elite CPU and ample 32GB of RAM, the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 excels as a general-purpose laptop, and it will run all day and into the night without needing to recharge. I like the solid and compact, all-metal design and the two OLED display options. Just be sure to compare pricing between Lenovo and Best Buy to find the best deal.
